expect.words: As in a dream, you see yourself tumbling down a great, dark staircase. All about you are shadowy images of struggles against fierce opponents and diabolical traps. These give way to another round of images: of imposing stone figures, a cool, clear lake, and, now, of an old, yet oddly youthful man. He turns toward you slowly, his long, silver hair dancing about him in a fresh breeze. "You have reached the final test, my friend! You are proved clever and powerful, but this is not yet enough! Seek me when you feel yourself worthy!" The dream dissolves around you as his last words echo through the void....
Endless Stair

You are at the bottom of a seemingly endless stair, winding its way upward beyond your vision. An eerie light, coming from all around you, casts strange shadows on the walls. To the south is a dark and winding trail.
Your old friend, the brass lantern, is at your feet.
Taken.

It is the brass lantern you have carried through two adventures already: battery-powered, dented in the places you remember, with a stout handle and a glass somebody has kept clean. It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.
The lamp is turned off.
The stairs are endless.
The lamp is now on.
Junction

You are at the junction of a north-south passage and an east-west passage. To the north, you can make out the bottom of a stairway. The ways to the east and south are relatively cramped, but a wider trail leads to the west.
Standing before you is a great rock. Imbedded within it is an Elvish sword.
The sword is deeply imbedded in the rock. You can't budge it.

A great rock, grey and rounded and older than the passage it stands in, which was cut round it rather than through it; whoever did the cutting had tried the other way first and given up. Imbedded in it, to half its length, is an Elvish sword, the hilt standing out at a height that invites a hand. The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.

It is an Elvish sword of great antiquity, long and light, with runes down the blade that you cannot read and a hilt worn to the shape of a hand, which, when you close yours on it, turns out to be yours. It is imbedded to half its length in the great rock, and looks as though it has been there since the rock was.
Barren Area

You are west of the junction, where the rock-bound passage widens out into a large, flat area. Although the land here is barren, you can see vegetation to the west. South of here is a mighty wall of stone, ancient and crumbling. To the southwest the wall has decayed enough to form an opening, through which seeps a thin mist. A trail dips sharply into rocky terrain to the northwest.
To the south the wall of stone, ancient and crumbling; everywhere else the cavern's own walls, far off and lost in the gloom, so that the flat barren land between seems wider than it is.
Cliff

This is a remarkable spot in the dungeon. Perhaps two hundred feet above you is a gaping hole in the earth's surface through which pours bright sunshine! A few seedlings from the world above, nurtured by the sunlight and occasional rains, have grown into giant trees, making this a virtual oasis in the desert of the Underground Empire. To the west is a sheer precipice, dropping nearly fifty feet to jagged rocks below. The way south is barred by a forbidding stone wall, crumbling from age. There is a jagged opening in the wall to the southwest, through which leaks a fine mist. The land to the east looks lifeless and barren.

A rope is tied to one of the large trees here and is dangling over the side of the cliff, reaching down to the shelf below. Among the trees, unless you are mistaken, something that is not a tree is keeping very still.
It seems as if somebody has been here recently, as there is some fresh bread lying beneath one of the other trees.

There seems to be nobody there, but it's hard to tell. Whatever it was, if it was anything, has the knack of being a trunk whenever you look straight at it, and of being a little to one side of where you looked when you look away. It is keeping very still, and it is not keeping still the way a tree does.
Taken.

A piece of waybread, flat and pale and fresh, of the kind Elves bake for a long road: a mouthful of it is a meal, and it keeps. Somebody left it under the tree not long ago, and did not come back for it, or has not yet.
You seem to hear, from the southwest, the sounds of the sea.

A long rope, tied to the trunk of one of the great trees with a knot that has thought about the matter, and dangling over the side of the cliff to the shelf below. It would hold you. It would hold several of you.
You seem to hear, from the southwest, the sounds of the sea.

A few seedlings from the world above, nurtured by the sunlight and the occasional rain that comes down the hole with it, have grown into giant trees, their trunks too wide to get your arms round and their tops lost in the light. They are the only things of their kind in the Empire, and they do not seem to know it.
There seems to be nobody there, but it's hard to tell.
Two hundred feet up, a hole in the earth's surface with the sky in it, and sunshine coming down through the hole. It is the best thing you have seen in three adventures and there is no way to it.
You take the rope in both hands and go down it, hand over hand, with the cliff face going by in front of your nose, to the shelf below.
Cliff Ledge

This is a rock-strewn ledge near the base of a tall cliff. The bottom of the cliff is another fifteen feet below. You have little hope of climbing up the cliff face, but you might be able to scramble down from here (though it's doubtful you could return).
A long piece of rope is dangling down from the top of the cliff and is within your reach.
A large chest, closed and locked, is lying among the boulders.
Far above you, at the brink of the cliff, something that is not a tree moves against the light, and the rope twitches once, as though somebody up there had a hand on it and had just taken it off.

A large chest of iron-bound wood, closed, and locked with a lock that has not been picked and will not be. It is heavy, and it has the look of a thing that somebody wants, and not the look of a thing that will open for you.
The chest is locked and cannot be opened. From somewhere above you, at the top of the cliff, somebody finds this funny, briefly, and stops.
The chest is now tied to the rope.
Time passes...

All at once, the chest is lifted from you. Looking up, you see a man at the top of the cliff, pulling intently at the rope. "That is uncommonly good of you, I do say!" He chuckles unpleasantly. "Oh, you are stuck, aren't you. Well, I'll be right back to get you!" He leaves your sight.
Cliff Ledge

This is a rock-strewn ledge near the base of a tall cliff. The bottom of the cliff is another fifteen feet below. You have little hope of climbing up the cliff face, but you might be able to scramble down from here (though it's doubtful you could return).
The rope has gone up the cliff with the chest. The man said he would be back in a short while; he did not say how short.
Time passes... Above you, the lock gives, and a lid goes back on a hinge that has not moved in a long time; and then a silence that is somebody looking. Nothing comes down the cliff yet.
Time passes... From the top of the cliff, a low whistle, of the kind a man gives at the sight of more than he was expecting. Nothing comes down the cliff.
Time passes... Above you, coins: counted, by the sound, one at a time, onto rock. The chest, it seems, had a good deal in it.
From the top of the cliff, between the sounds of a chest being gone through, a voice calls down: "Still there? Good. I said a short while, and a short while is what I meant; keep your shirt on."
Time passes... A pause above. Then footsteps, up there, going away from the brink, and the sound of things being gathered up. He is not gone; you can still hear him.
Time passes... Footsteps, going away from the brink and coming back to it, the way a man paces who is deciding something, and deciding it in his own favour.
Time passes... The footsteps come back to the brink and stop there. Nothing is said; somebody is looking down at you, and taking his time about it.
Time passes... Something scrapes on the rock at the top, where the rope is tied, and a coil of it shifts against the edge; he is not long now.
Time passes...
A familiar voice calls down to you. "Are you still there?" he bellows with a coarse laugh. "Well, then, grab onto the rope and we'll see what we can do." The rope drops to within your reach.
You grab securely on to the rope.

The man starts to heave on the rope and within a few moments you arrive at the top of the cliff. The man removes the last few valuables from the chest and prepares to leave. "You've been a good sport! Here, take this, for whatever good it is! I can't see that I'll be needing one!" He hands you a plain wooden staff from the bottom of the chest and begins examining his valuables.
The chest, open and empty, is at your feet.
Cliff
Your "friend" from the cliff is here, with a number of valuables under one arm, going through them with great attention.
There is a chest here, open and empty.
(You have been here before, so only the room's name is given. LOOK describes it again; VERBOSE describes every room in full every time, and BRIEF puts it back.)

A plain wooden staff, a little taller than you are, worn smooth where a hand has held it for a very long time. It is the kind of staff an old man leans on, and it has, somewhere about it, the look of one you have seen before, in a dream.
You seem to hear, from the southwest, the sounds of the sea.
Your "friend", moving quickly, dodges behind some trees and is lost from sight.
You can't see any such thing.
You can't see any such thing.
Land of Shadow

You are standing atop a steep cliff, looking west over a vast ocean. Far below, the surf pounds at a sandy beach. To the south and east are rolling hills filled with eerie shadows. A path cut into the face of the cliff descends toward the beach. To the north is a tall stone wall, which ends at the cliff edge. It was obviously built long ago, and directly north is a spot where you could climb over the rubble of the decaying wall.
Flathead Ocean

You are at the shore of an amazing underground sea, the topic of many a legend among adventurers. Few were known to have arrived at this spot, and fewer to return. There is a heavy surf and a breeze is blowing onshore. The land rises steeply to the east and quicksand prevents movement to the south. A thick mist covers the ocean and extends over the hills to the east. A path heads north along the beach.

An underground sea, the topic of many a legend among adventurers: grey water under a grey mist, with no far shore and no horizon, and a heavy surf coming in out of the mist as though it had been coming in since the Empire fell and meant to go on after. The Flatheads named it for themselves. It is big enough to carry the name.
Time passes...
Cliff Base

You are at the base of a steep cliff. Directly above you is a wide ledge and far above that some natural sunlight can be seen. To the northeast is a steeply climbing path and the ground becomes sandy toward the south.
Hairpin Loop

You are at a sharp turn on a narrow and steeply sloping path, strewn with boulders of various sizes. The path climbs sharply toward a desolate plain to the southeast. Southwest of here the path winds down to the base of a cliff.
Barren Area
Junction
Standing before you is a great rock. Imbedded within it is an Elvish sword.
Damp Passage

This is a particularly damp spot even by dungeon standards. You can see the junction to the west, and two similar passages to the east and northeast. A wide stone channel steeply descends into the room from the south. It is covered with slippery moss and lichen. The channel crosses the room, but the opening where it once continued north is now blocked by rubble.
Dead End
You have come to the end of two adjoining passages to the west and the northwest.
You search the place, which is to say you look at it closely, and it looks like this: Dead End
You have come to the end of two adjoining passages to the west and the northwest.
Engravings Room
You are in a room with passages heading southwest and southeast. The north wall is ornately carved, filled with strange runes and writing in an unfamiliar language.
An old and wizened man is huddled, asleep, in the corner. He is snoring loudly, and looks quite weak and frail.
The runes are in an ancient language. Some pictures among the runes depict flames, stone statues, and an old man.
The old man is roused to consciousness. He peers at you through eyes which appear much younger and stronger than his frail body and waits, as if expecting something to happen.

He looks up at you and takes the waybread. Slowly, he eats the bread and pauses when he is finished. He starts to speak: "Perhaps what you seek is through there!" He points at the carved wall to the north, where you now notice the bare outline of a secret door. When you turn back, the old man is gone!
The massive stone door opens noiselessly. Beyond the secret door are dark, forbidding stairs leading down to a passage below. Flickering torchlight illuminates the passage.
You go through the secret door and down the dark, forbidding stairs, toward the flickering torchlight below.
Button Room

You are at the southern end of a long hall. To the south, stairs ascend into darkness. To the north the corridor is illuminated by torches set high in the walls, out of reach. On one wall is a red button.
A red button, set in the wall at the height of a hand, with nothing written near it to say what it does. It has been pushed before; the red is worn through to brass at the middle.
Your potential is 1 of a possible 7, in 52 moves.
Engravings Room
Dead End
You can't go that way.
Engravings Room
Damp Passage
The channel is too steep and the moss too slippery.
Junction
Standing before you is a great rock. Imbedded within it is an Elvish sword.
Creepy Crawl
You are in a dark and quite creepy crawlway with passages leaving to the north, east, south, and southwest.
Tight Squeeze
This is a very low and narrow passage leading east to west.
Crystal Grotto

This is a chamber of breathtaking beauty. Mighty stalagmites form crystalline-encrusted rock formations. Phosphorescent mosses, fed by a trickle of water from above, make the crystals glow and sparkle with every color of the rainbow. There is an opening to the west, and a man-made passage heads south.

Stalagmites, each the work of ten thousand years of dripping, grown together into formations the size of houses and crusted over with crystal, and the crystal lit from inside by the moss so that every facet of it is a different colour. It is the most beautiful thing underground, and nobody built it, which may be the point.
Royal Hall

This is the north end of a large hall with a vaulted ceiling. A long, tiled hallway leads north through a tall arch. Although the purpose of this room is unclear, there is a large rendering of the Royal Seal of Lord Dimwit Flathead carved on the wall.
The Seal is vintage Flathead, with signs of excess nearly everywhere. It shows a curiously flat-headed figure wearing a gaudy crown, surrounded by the Crown Jewels of the Empire.
Great Door

You are in the southern half of a monumental hall. To the east lies a tremendous iron door which appears to be rusted shut. The rock beside the door is cracked and strained, as though it had been holding something back for a long time and was tiring of it.
The iron door is rusted shut and cannot be opened.

To the right of the iron door the rock of the wall is cracked from the floor to the vault, the cracks dark and wide enough to put a finger in, and running the way cracks run in a thing that is being pushed from behind. Dust sifts out of them now and then, without any reason you can see. The door is for ever; the rock, by the look of it, is not, and a good shake of the earth would settle the matter. Nothing smaller will.
You can't go that way.
Royal Hall
Crystal Grotto
Tight Squeeze
Creepy Crawl
Foggy Room
You are in a dank passage filled with a wispy fog. A spooky passageway leads north and a wider path heads off to the south. To the west, the path leaves the rock and enters an eerie, shadowy land.
Lake Shore

You are in a wide cavern on the north shore of a small lake. Some polished stone steps lead to the southeast and a sheer rock face prevents any movement around the lake to the southwest. The cavern is dimly lit from above. The water has the look of a cold that would open your hands for you, and would not give back what fell out of them; everything in your hands goes to the bottom, not the light and the sword only but every last thing you carry, and whatever you cannot afford to lose there had better be left on the shore, which is lit, after its fashion, and will keep it. What you wear, it leaves you.

The light you carry throws your shadow on the water, which does not want it: a lamp goes under here, lit or dark, and comes up a dead one, and the shore is where it should be left, with everything else in your hands.
Aqueduct View

This is a small balcony carved into a near-vertical cliff. To the east, stretching from north to south, stands a monumental aqueduct supported by mighty stone pillars, some of which are starting to crumble from age. You feel a sense of loss and sadness as you ponder this once-proud structure and the failure of the Empire which created this and other engineering marvels. Some stone steps lead up to the northwest.

The aqueduct is large and impressive. It was probably the major method of water transport in the Empire. It strides from north to south across the gorge on arches that would hold up a city, and did; and here and there a pillar has begun to go, and the arch above it with it, and the channel on top carries nothing now but moss and a little rain. It is the saddest thing you have seen underground, and you have seen some sad things.
Lake Shore

The light you carry throws your shadow on the water, which does not want it: a lamp goes under here, lit or dark, and comes up a dead one, and the shore is where it should be left, with everything else in your hands.

A small lake, dark and very still, in a wide cavern dimly lit from above, with polished stone steps going down toward it to the southeast and a sheer rock face closing off the shore to the southwest. It does not look warm. It looks, in fact, like the kind of cold that opens a hand whether its owner likes it or not, and anyone going in would do well to leave on the shore whatever they cannot afford to have at the bottom, which is to say everything in their hands, the sword as much as the light and the rest with them; the shore is lit, after its fashion, and will keep it. It does not look deep, either, though a lake that still keeps its secrets at this age may be expected to keep that one.
lamp: Dropped.
wooden staff: Dropped.
Go jump in a lake!
You are nearly paralyzed by the icy waters as you swim into the center of the lake.
On the Lake

You are floating on the surface of the lake. The water is ice cold and your ability to survive here for long is very questionable. A swim north puts you at your starting point. Conditions to the east are poor where the lake turns into swamp. The west and south shores are suitable for walking, however.
You take a breath and go under.
Underwater

You are below the surface of the lake. It turns out that the lake is quite shallow and the bottom is only a few feet below you. Considering the frigid temperature of the water, you should probably not plan an extended stay. The lake bottom is sandy and a few hearty plants and algae live there.
Out of the corner of your eye, a small, shiny object appears in the sand. A moment later, it is gone!
You don't come across anything unusual, although something in it, now and then, catches the light.
Something sparkling in the sand catches your eye for a moment.
There is a great tremor from within the earth. The entire dungeon shakes violently and loose debris falls from above you.
The shiny object slips from your grasp and back onto the floor of the lake, where it is covered in sand. It is still there, under the sand, within reach of another try.
Out of the corner of your eye, a small, shiny object appears in the sand. A moment later, it is gone!
The icy waters are taking their toll. You will not be able to hold out much longer.
You run out of air and return to the surface.
On the Lake
You take a breath and go under.
Underwater
Something sparkling in the sand catches your eye for a moment.
The shiny object slips from your grasp and back onto the floor of the lake, where it is covered in sand. It is still there, under the sand, within reach of another try.
You catch a brief glimpse of something shiny in the sand.
You are becoming very weak. You had better leave the water before you drown!
The shiny object slips from your grasp and back onto the floor of the lake, where it is covered in sand. It is still there, under the sand, within reach of another try.
You catch a brief glimpse of something shiny in the sand.
You run out of air and return to the surface.
On the Lake
Southern Shore

You are on the south shore of the lake. Rock formations prevent movement to the west and thickening swamp to the east makes the going all but impossible. To the south, where the beach meets a rock formation, you can make out a dark passage sloping steeply upward into the rock. The dark in it is not the ordinary kind that a lamp answers, and no lamp comes across the lake lit in any case; what keeps a grue off a person is sold in a can, and the can is somewhere a light has already been.
You are nearly paralyzed by the icy waters as you swim into the center of the lake.
On the Lake
Western Shore

You are on the western shore of the lake. The ground here is quite hard, but a few sickly reeds manage to grow near the water's edge. The only path leads into the rock to the south. The water is the same water as on the north shore, as cold and as still, and it will open your hands as readily from this side; a flame least of all comes out of it burning. No light crosses this lake alight, from either shore; whatever is to be had on the far side in the dark will have to be got some other way than by carrying a light to it. What you cannot lose to the bottom had better be left on the hard ground here, which is lit, after its fashion, from the south.
Scenic Vista

You are in a small chamber carved in the rock, with the sole exit to the north. Mounted on one wall is a table labelled "Scenic Vista," whose featureless surface is angled toward you. One might believe that the table was used to indicate points of interest in the view from this spot, like those found in many parks. On the other hand, your surroundings are far from spacious and by no stretch of the imagination could this spot be considered scenic. An indicator above the table reads "III".
Mounted on one wall is a flaming torch, which fills the room with a flickering light.
The surface is pale and featureless, but slowly, an image takes shape!
You see a wide room with two nearly identical passages leading east and northeast. A wide channel descends steeply into the room and seems to be blocked by rubble.

The image slowly fades, and the pale surface, angled toward you, seems to lean a little nearer as it goes, the way a thing does that would rather be touched than looked at. The places it shows are underground, and have no sun of their own; and the flame on the wall beside it is the one light in this room that has not been near the water.
Taken.
The indicator above the table flickers briefly, then changes to "IV".
The surface is pale and featureless, but slowly, an image takes shape!

You see the interior of a huge temple rudely constructed of basalt blocks. Flickering torches cast a sallow illumination over an altar still wet with the blood of human sacrifice, its velvet covers stained and encrusted with gore.
The image slowly fades. The surface, for once, seems content to be looked at.
The surface is pale and featureless, but slowly, an image takes shape!

You see the interior of a huge temple rudely constructed of basalt blocks. Flickering torches cast a sallow illumination over an altar still wet with the blood of human sacrifice, its velvet covers stained and encrusted with gore.
The image slowly fades. The surface, for once, seems content to be looked at.
Time passes... The image under the surface is stirring now, going thin at the edges; the indicator will not be long.

The surface is pale and featureless, and stays so. Above it the indicator is flickering, the way it does when it is about to change, and the table shows nothing until the indicator has settled on what it is to show. Look again in a moment.
The indicator above the table flickers briefly, then changes to "I".
The surface is pale and featureless, but slowly, an image takes shape!
You see a passage cluttered with broken timbers. An extremely narrow opening can be seen at the end of the room.
The image slowly fades, and the pale surface, angled toward you, seems to lean a little nearer as it goes, the way a thing does that would rather be touched than looked at.
You touch the table and are instantly transported to another place!
Timber Room

This is a long and narrow passage, which is cluttered with broken timbers. A wide passage comes from the east and turns at the west end of the room into a very narrow passageway. From the west comes a strong draft.
There is a pile of broken timbers here.
You can't search the broken timber.

You cannot fit through this passage with that load. The passageway takes nothing through it bigger than your hand: not the lamp, not the torch, not the sword; a person, and what a person can close a fist on, and no more.
Ladder Bottom
This is a rather wide room. On one side is the bottom of a narrow wooden ladder. To the west and the south are passages leaving the room.
You suddenly find yourself back in the viewing room!
Scenic Vista
The surface is pale and featureless, but slowly, an image takes shape!
You see a tiny room with rough walls. Chiseled crudely on one wall is the number "8". In one corner is a spray can, its label too small to read from here. The only apparent exit seems to be a blur.
The image slowly fades, and the pale surface, angled toward you, seems to lean a little nearer as it goes, the way a thing does that would rather be touched than looked at.
You touch the table and are instantly transported to another place!
Room 8

This is a small chamber carved out of the rock at the end of a short crawl. On the wall is crudely chiseled the number "8". The only apparent exit, to the east, seems to be a blur and a loud, whirring sound resounds through the rock.
A spray can is in the corner. In large type is the legend "Frobozz Magic Grue Repellent."
Taken.

A spray can, dented, of the kind the Frobozz Magic Company sold to adventurers who were going to need it and to everyone else who was not. The legend on it is in large type, with instructions under it in small, and the small print is the Company's one moment of candour: the can holds a single application, and an application is good for a few minutes of a grue's good manners, which the label calls unpredictable and you would do well to call short: about as long, it says, as it takes to get from a water's edge to the top of a slope, so that the place to spray is the edge, with the hands already empty. There is a slosh in it when it is moved: one slosh, one spraying.
You suddenly find yourself back in the viewing room!
Scenic Vista
You can't go that way.
Western Shore

The light you carry lies on the water, and the water would take it as readily from this side as from the other; no flame or lamp crosses this lake alight. What has to be carried across it is carried another way.
Dropped.
The spray smells like a mixture of old socks and burning rubber. If I were a grue I'd sure stay clear!
Dropped.
You are nearly paralyzed by the icy waters as you swim into the center of the lake.
On the Lake
The smell is holding, for the moment: it is good for about as long as the climb takes, if you do not dawdle on the beach.
Southern Shore

You have moved into a dark place, and a thicker dark than the usual kind: it has a smell, and a sound in it of breathing, and more than one of each. Whatever is said of grues elsewhere, here they are not a likelihood.
It is pitch black. You are likely to be eaten by a grue.
That horrible smell is much less pungent now, which is to say it is nearly gone, and the dark up the slope, which kept its distance while it lasted, has noticed.
Oh, no! Dozens of lurking grues attack and devour you! You must have stumbled into an authentic grue lair!
**** You have died ****

You find yourself deep within the earth in a barren prison cell. Outside the iron-barred window, you can see a great, fiery pit. Flames leap up and very nearly sear your flesh. After a while, footfalls can be heard in the distance, then closer and closer....
The door swings open, and in walks an old man.

He is dressed simply in a hood and cloak, wearing an amulet and ring, carrying an old book under one arm, and leaning on a wooden staff. A single key, as if to a massive prison cell, hangs from his belt.
He raises the staff toward you and you hear him speak, as if in a dream: "I await you, though your journey be long and full of peril. Go then, and let me not wait long!"

You feel some great power well up inside you and you fall to the floor. The next moment, you are awakening, as if from a deep slumber. What you were carrying is not with you: the old man scatters what a visitor brings him, and it is lying where he left it, somewhere along the way in, between the stair and the lake, with the lamp alone brought back to your feet.
Endless Stair
There is a brass lantern here (providing light).
Taken.
Junction
Standing before you is a great rock. Imbedded within it is an Elvish sword.
The sword is deeply imbedded in the rock. You can't budge it.
Creepy Crawl
Tight Squeeze
Crystal Grotto
Royal Hall
Great Door
Great Door

This is the south end of a monumental hall, full of debris from a recent earthquake. To the east is a great iron door, rusted shut. To its right, however, is a gaping cleft in the rock and behind, a cleared area.
Museum Entrance

This is the entrance to the Royal Museum, the finest and grandest in the Great Underground Empire. To the south, down a few steps, is the entrance to the Royal Puzzle and to the east, through a stone door, is the Royal Jewel Collection. A wooden door to the north is open and leads to the Museum of Technology. To the west is a great iron door, rusted shut. To its left, however, is a cleft in the rock providing an exit from the museum.
The stone door is closed.
The door is now open.
Technology Museum
This is a large hall which hosted the technological exhibits of the Great Underground Empire. A door to the south is open.

A strange grey machine, shaped somewhat like a clothes dryer, is on one side of the room. On the other side of the hall is a powerful-looking black machine, a tight tangle of wires, pipes, and motors. A plaque is mounted near the door. The writing is faded, however, and cannot be made out clearly. The two machines seem to be in bad shape, rusting in many spots.

Directly in front of you is a large golden machine, which has a seat with a console in front. On the console is a single button and a dial connected to a three-digit display which reads 948. The machine is surprisingly shiny and shows few signs of age.
The words cannot be made out.

The machine consists of a seat and a console containing one small button and a dial connected to a display which reads 948. It stands on the floor and not on a plinth, and the floor round it is scuffed in long arcs toward the door, as though it had been moved before and could be again; a hand on it rocks it a little. It would go where it was pushed.

A strange grey machine, shaped somewhat like a clothes dryer, with a lid and a switch and the look of a thing you have seen before, in a mine, in another adventure, where it turned coal into something better. This one turns nothing into anything; it is rusting in many spots, and has not been asked to in a long time.

Inside Mirror
You are inside a rectangular box of wood whose structure is rather complicated. Four sides and the roof are filled in, and the floor is open.

As you face the side opposite the entrance, two short sides of carved and polished wood are to your left and right. The left panel is mahogany, the right pine. The wall you face is red on its left half and black on its right. On the entrance side, the wall is white opposite the red part of the wall it faces, and yellow opposite the black section. The painted walls are at least twice the length of the unpainted ones. The ceiling is painted blue.

In the floor is a stone channel about six inches wide and a foot deep. The channel is oriented in a north-south direction. In the exact center of the room the channel widens into a circular depression perhaps two feet wide. Incised in the stone around this area is a compass rose.

Running from one short wall to the other at about waist height is a wooden bar, carefully carved and drilled. This bar is pierced in two places. The first hole is in the center of the bar (and thus the center of the room). The second is at the left end of the room (as you face opposite the entrance). Through each hole runs a wooden pole.
The pole at the left end of the bar is short, extending about a foot above the bar, and ends in a hand grip. The pole has been dropped into a hole carved in the stone floor.

The long pole at the center of the bar extends from the ceiling through the bar to the circular area in the stone channel. This bottom end of the pole has a T-bar a bit less than two feet long attached to it, and on the T-bar is carved an arrow. The arrow and T-bar are pointing west.
The mirror on the entrance side stands open, and the hallway shows through it.
The pole is now slightly above the floor.
The structure rotates clockwise.
The arrow on the compass rose now indicates northwest.
The structure rotates clockwise.
The arrow on the compass rose now indicates north.
The mirror quietly swings shut.
The pole is lowered into the channel.
The pine wall swings open.

You feel yourself disembodied in a deep blackness. A voice from the void speaks: "I have waited a long age for you, my friend, but perhaps it has been another that I have been seeking. Good night, oh worthy adventurer!" It is the last you hear.
Void

A deep blackness, in which you are not so much standing as suspended. The voice has gone, and the Empire with it. Nothing further will happen to you in this game; whoever the old man was waiting for, he has gone to look for them elsewhere.
